recent_posts.title: Guest Post: Announcing the 2026 Rust-Edu Refresh and CFP
recent_posts.summary: Rust-Edu, a community-led initiative promoting Rust in academic environments, is undergoing a revitalization led by Bart Massey and Mordecai Etukudo. The refresh aims to rebuild the organization into a more structured and collaborative effort. A Call for Participation (CFP) is open for educators, developers, students, and community builders to join the Rust-Edu Organizing Committee and help shape how Rust is taught in universities worldwide. Contributors can connect via the Rust-Edu Zulip chat.

recent_posts.title: Rust Foundation and Package Registry Leaders Unite to Address Open Source Sustainability Crisis
recent_posts.summary: The Rust Foundation has joined as a founding member of the newly-formed Sustaining Package Registries Working Group under the Linux Foundation. The group brings together package registry leaders to tackle the financial, operational, and security challenges of running public registries at global scale. With open source downloads approaching 10 trillion in 2025 and AI-driven demand accelerating bot traffic and abuse, registries face a growing sustainability gap. The working group aims to develop shared funding models, coordinated security practices, governance frameworks, and ecosystem education to treat registry sustainability as a shared industry responsibility.

recent_posts.title: Project Director Update — March 2026
recent_posts.summary: The Rust Foundation's Project Directors recap the March 10, 2026 board meeting. Key highlights include a proposal for an AI-focused research initiative, the Symposium project joining the Rust Innovation Lab, early discussions on making crates.io more sustainable and a potential Rust Ecosystem Fund, Canonical joining as a Gold member, the Foundation joining Datadog's Open Source Program, ongoing work to address typosquatting attacks on crates.io, progress on the C++ interop initiative, and RustConf 2026 schedule and ticket announcements including travel grants for active Rust project members.

recent_posts.title: Rust Foundation CEO on funding, regulation, and open source survival
recent_posts.summary: ExpressVPN's Pete Membrey interviews Dr. Rebecca Rumbul, CEO of the Rust Foundation, about the sustainability challenges facing open source infrastructure. Key topics include crates.io's explosive growth (100B to 250B downloads in months, pushing 5 petabytes/month with projections of 18PB by end of next year), the precarious reliance on donated cloud credits, and the Rust Foundation's successful lobbying to create a new 'Open Source Steward' legal category under the EU Cyber Resilience Act. Dr. Rumbul argues that major tech companies must treat open-source funding as a core operational expense rather than charity. The conversation also covers Rust's industry adoption (Google's 70% reduction in Android memory safety bugs), Rust's growing role as the engine beneath Python-based AI workloads, and career advice for developers to contribute to open source projects.

recent_posts.title: Welcoming Symposium to the Rust Innovation Lab
recent_posts.summary: The Rust Foundation's Rust Innovation Lab (RIL) has welcomed Symposium as its second board-approved project. Symposium is a tool that automatically installs skills, MCP servers, and other extensions based on the dependencies in a Rust crate, helping AI agents work more effectively with Rust projects. Led by Niko Matsakis (Rust language design team co-lead), Symposium aims to bring Rust's principles of interoperability and vendor neutrality to agentic development. It uses a centralized recommendations repository where crate authors can define plugins that identify appropriate extensions for their crates, with plans to eventually allow crates to package plugins directly.

recent_posts.title: RustConf 2026: Speakers Announced, Registration Open
recent_posts.summary: RustConf 2026 registration is now open, with the conference scheduled for September 8-11 in Montreal (plus an online option). The program features an expanded schedule with a new track, Community Lightning Talks, and Project Updates sessions. Highlighted keynotes include Jon Seager covering Rust adoption in Ubuntu (including Rust-based rewrites of coreutils and sudo), and a closing fireside chat between Rust Foundation CEO Rebecca Rumbul and Python Software Foundation ED Deb Nicholson on open source governance, security, and cross-ecosystem interoperability.

recent_posts.title: Rust Foundation Interop Initiative Update: From Research to Implementation
recent_posts.summary: The Rust Foundation's Interop Initiative is transitioning from research to implementation, focusing on improving Rust–C++ interoperability. After publishing a formal problem statement and engaging with the C++ standards committee (WG21/ISO), the Foundation concluded that near-term practical improvements are more impactful than waiting for broad memory-safe C++ standardization (which could take until 2029+). A contractor (Teor) has been engaged to advance the Rust/C++ Interop Problem Space Mapping goal, coordinate working groups, and support tooling and infrastructure improvements for mixed-language development environments.

recent_posts.title: What’s Next for the Rust Innovation Lab?
recent_posts.summary: The Rust Foundation outlines the direction of its Rust Innovation Lab (RIL), a program that hosts and funds Rust projects filling ecosystem gaps or showcasing Rust's strengths. The RIL's inaugural project, rustls (a memory-safe TLS implementation), is highlighted as a model candidate. The Foundation describes three criteria for RIL projects: showcasing Rust's strengths, filling developer needs, and benefiting uniquely from Foundation support. Projects can be mature or experimental, temporary or permanent residents of the Lab, and receive funding, security guidance, marketing, and developer recruitment support. Maintainers of qualifying projects are encouraged to apply.

recent_posts.title: Canonical Joins the Rust Foundation as a Gold Member
recent_posts.summary: Canonical, the publisher of Ubuntu, has joined the Rust Foundation as a Gold Member. The membership reflects Canonical's growing investment in Rust, which now powers core Ubuntu system components including replacements for coreutils and sudo. Canonical's VP Engineering highlighted particular interest in crates.io security and reducing unknown dependencies for async, HTTP, and cryptography in regulated environments. The move signals Rust's expanding role in large-scale production systems and Linux infrastructure.

recent_posts.title: Guest Blog: FOSDEM 2026 — Rust Devroom in Review
recent_posts.summary: FOSDEM 2026's Rust Devroom featured 16 talks covering embedded systems, game development, and server-side applications, marking 10 years of Rust presence at the event. The organizers note a shift from talks about Rust's potential to real-world adoption stories, with projects increasingly replacing components with Rust to address bugs, performance, and stability issues. The devroom attracted hundreds of attendees in a 500+ seat venue, reflecting Rust's growing integration across the open source ecosystem.
